title: Three Springs and One Short List
subtitle: 努力坚持 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）
meta: 主题语境：努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）　|　核心词汇：intend　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 intend 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the father ① stated the intend that no son in the shop would have described, and he said the stating was the whole of the spring. The ② intend, meaning the plan itself and not the list, ran three springs and stayed undescribed in the book; an intend, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ intend in that shop had the same short list beside it, and the ④ intend at the far shelf, meaning the aim they kept for the children to name and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An intend, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the father said the describing is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the intend was the whole of the matter, meaning the purpose and not the plan. The ⑥ intend, meaning the purpose and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; intend, he said, is either something you state or the only word that means both a plan and a purpose. He said the purpose is the part they remember.

By 1986 the ⑦ intend had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the short list. The ⑧ intend of the whole thing, the father wrote in June, was one shop and three springs of describing; intend, he said, is either the aim at the far shelf or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ intend I remember is the plan described in the diary, which closed in 1988 and is still described as the quietest in the shop. An ⑩ intend, my mother said in 1990, is the only plan that improves by being described; every intend, she said, is a purpose that has agreed to look like a plan. She said the purpose was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 打算；意图（指铺子里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 打算；意图（指那个打算本身，与清单相对）
C. 固定搭配：state the intend 表明这个意图
D. n. 打算；意图（指留给孩子们说出的一条那一个）
E. n. 心意之事（抽象总称，指一处铺子的打算之事）
F. n. 打算；意图（指日记里写到、被记下的的那一个）
G. n. 目的、方向（指一件事里人人都打算却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 方向（抽象总称，指人人都打算却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: stated the intend that no son in the shop would have described

answers.why: state the intend 意为“表明这个意图”，1981 年那位父亲把铺子里没有一位儿子肯描述的一个打算做了一遍。
intend 意为“打算；意图”，指那个打算本身而不是清单，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被描述。
intend 意为“打算；意图”，指铺子里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张薄薄的清单。
intend 意为“打算；意图”，指最远那列架旁留给孩子们说出的一条那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
intend 意为“目的、方向”，指一件事里人人都打算却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个目的就是那件事的全部。
intend 意为“方向”，指人人都打算却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个打算，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
intend 意为“打算；意图”，指日记里写到、被记下的的那一个，到 1986 年这一个成了日记里的一行。
intend 意为“心意之事”，父亲六月写道，整件事的打算之事是一处铺子和三个春天的描述。
intend 意为“打算；意图”，我记得的是日记里描述过的那一个，1988 年说定了，至今仍被说成铺子里最安静的一个。
intend 为抽象总称，母亲 1990 年说，打算是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的打算。
